heading: INT. FAMILY HOME - DINING ROOM - AFTER THE FUNERAL

units.text: INT. FAMILY HOME - DINING ROOM - AFTER THE FUNERAL
Casserole dishes crowd the long walnut table, foil peeled back, forks standing in them like flags in captured ground.
The guests have gone.
Only the photographs remain, a hundred faces watching from the sideboard.
AUGUSTINE PELLEGRINI, seventies, stiff in his black suit, stands at the head of the table counting plates.
His daughter PHILIPPA, forties, leans in the doorway still wearing her coat and her black gloves, keys in her fist like a dagger.
Thank you all for coming. Truly. Your kindness is a comfort.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: Dad. They've left.
units.name: PHILIPPA

units.text: Eddie, will you have more of the ham?
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: Philippa pulls her gloves off one finger at a time.
Her father stacks two plates, sets down a third, picks up a fourth, and arranges them in a tower that shivers under his shaking hand.
She crosses to him.
He steps aside, and she takes the stack and slides it back onto the table.
He takes it again.
She takes it back.
They stand, hands on china, eye to eye, neither letting go.
She isn't coming home, Dad.
units.name: PHILIPPA

units.text: Two years of pills in the green bowl.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: Dad.
units.name: PHILIPPA

units.text: You were in Denver!
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: The plates slip.
They crash.
The sound rolls through the house and out into the quiet street, and neither of them moves to pick up a single shard.
